title: Lesson 10: Speaking and Listening: Patterns of the Stars
objective: Students will use notes about star patterns to participate in a Science Talk, record observations in a notebook, and reflect on integrity during discussions.

what_is_taught.skill: review information from an anchor chart
identify important information to answer a question
share ideas with a partner using polite communication
record notes with words and sketches to explain a scientific question
use sentence frames to build onto others' ideas during a group discussion
participate in a structured Science Talk protocol in small groups
reflect on personal behavior and integrity during group discussions
record observations of images and videos in a notebook using descriptive language
use language supports such as sentence frames and word walls to aid communication and writing

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify important information from anchor charts and notes
student_actions.oral_production: share ideas with partners and groups using sentence frames
student_actions.written_production: write notes and observations in notes sheets and notebooks
student_actions.procedural_application: participate in Science Talk protocol using sentence frames
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain reasoning for notes and ideas during partner and group discussions

evidence.quote: Direct students' attention to the Patterns of the Stars anchor chart and review the big ideas.
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner: 'What information do you think is most important to know when answering the question 'Why can't we see stars during the day?''
Circulate and listen in as students share with their partner.
Tell students that now they will record their own notes about why we can't see stars during the day, and they might want to include a note, or notes, like the one starred on the anchor chart.
Display the Patterns of the Stars notes sheet and read the prompt aloud: -'Why can't we see stars during the day?'
Tell students they may begin writing their own notes to answer the question: Focus students on the prompt. Reread it aloud and invite them to begin writing their individual notes.
Circulate and support students as they write. Remind them to use the Patterns of the Moon anchor chart and Sun, Moon, and Stars Word Wall to help them while writing.
-'Why can't we see stars during the day?'
Remind them that they used this protocol in Lessons 6 and 8 and review as necessary using the Science Talk Protocol anchor chart.

Remind students of the sentence frames during the previous Science Talks: 'I think he/she means __________.' 'I'd like to add ________.' 'This makes me think __________.' Invite students to repeat each sentence frame as you read it aloud.
Guide students through the protocol. Circulate and use the Speaking and Listening Checklist to track student progress. Prompt students with questions to help them expand on their ideas.
Refocus whole group and collect students' notes sheets.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group: 'What does it mean to have integrity?' (to do the right thing even when it's hard)
Invite students to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner: 'What is one way you noticed yourself or a classmate showing integrity during the Science Talk protocol?'
Ask students to return to their seats. Share a few great examples of integrity that you heard while listening to students talk.
Direct students' attention to the learning targets and read the second one aloud: 'I can record my observations of videos/images of the sky in the Sky notebook.'
Display pages 9-10 of the Sky notebook and sun photograph 7 and use the same process as in previous lessons to distribute notebooks and colored pencils and to guide students to complete this page.
Signal all students to stop writing through the use of a designated sound and collect their Sky notebooks.

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Models reviewing anchor charts, using sentence frames for discussion, and writing notes with sketches.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What information do you think is most important to know when answering the question 'Why can't we see stars during the day?'
What does it mean to have integrity?
What is one way you noticed yourself or a classmate showing integrity during the Science Talk protocol?

scope.breadth: Uses multiple instructional blocks to develop speaking, listening, and writing skills related to scientific observation and discussion.
scope.depth: Focuses on using notes to support oral discussion and reflection on integrity, with scaffolds for language and writing.

context.stimulus_provided: anchor charts, notes sheets, photographs, word walls

sections_covered.warm_up: Review Patterns of the Stars anchor chart and discuss important information.
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Model use of sentence frames and note-taking strategies.
sections_covered.guided_practice: Participate in Science Talk protocol in small groups using notes and sentence frames.
sections_covered.independent_application: Write observations in Sky notebook independently.
sections_covered.check_for_understanding: Reflect on integrity and use of evidence during Science Talk.
sections_covered.differentiated_reinforce: Provide guided notes sheets and sentence frames for ELLs and students needing support.
sections_covered.differentiated_extend: Encourage ELLs to verbalize thinking with peers and use home language support.

supports.english_language_learners: Rephrase complex questions, provide sentence frames, group students strategically, label photographs, and encourage verbalizing thinking.
supports.universal_design_udl: Use total participation techniques, provide supportive writing tools, and offer multiple ways to respond.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Provide partially filled-in notes sheets and guided writing support.
supports.above_level_extend: Encourage use of sentence frames to build on others' ideas and explain reasoning during discussions.

assessment.method: Observation of participation in Science Talk and review of notes and Sky notebook entries.

materials: Patterns of the Stars anchor chart (begun in Lesson 7)
Patterns of the Stars notes sheet (one per student and one to display)
Sun, Moon, and Stars Word Wall (begun in Unit 1, Lesson 1)
Does the Sun Sleep?: Noticing Sun, Moon, and Star Patterns (one to display)
Science Talk Protocol anchor chart (begun in Lesson 6)
Speaking and Listening Checklist (for teacher reference; see Assessment Overview and Resources)
Unit 2 Guiding Question anchor chart (begun in Lesson 2; added to during Work Time C; see supporting materials)
Working to Become Ethical People anchor chart (begun in Unit 1, Lesson 4)

notes: The lesson integrates speaking, listening, and writing around a science topic, emphasizing use of evidence and respectful communication. Supports for ELLs and students needing additional help are embedded throughout.
